title: The Orchard of Maple Hollow
premise: Beatrix Nystrom, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter scraping out a quiet life in the coastal village of Maple Hollow, hires a charming stranger to pose as her boyfriend for a family reunion she dreads. The stranger, Elias Ward, is actually an investigator hunting the orchard's new owner, who is quietly defrauding the town's elderly landholders — including Beatrix's grandmother. Falling for each other for real, they must expose the scheme outside the courts, where the law has failed Maple Hollow before, while deciding whether Beatrix can let a man with secrets belong in the life she rebuilt. In the end, the town confronts the fraudster together, Elias chooses to stay after his last train home has already gone, and Beatrix finishes her novel — and opens her door.
about_author: Dominic Almeida is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering land disputes and county fairs before turning to fiction. They write love stories set in places where everyone knows your name and half your mistakes.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Five years after a public humiliation drove her from the city, Beatrix tends the decommissioned lighthouse and drafts a novel she's afraid to finish. When her mother announces a family reunion — with the cousin who betrayed her attending — Beatrix panics. Emotional beat: restless safety, the ache of a life too small to hold her.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ferry Dock
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Elias Ward arrives asking odd questions about the orchard's new owner, and Beatrix, mistaking his interest for availability, impulsively hires him as her fake boyfriend for the reunion. He agrees too easily. Emotional beat: reckless hope disguised as a practical transaction; first spark of real chemistry.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The reunion unfolds: Beatrix's cousin needling her, her grandmother Maren holding court, Elias performing the boyfriend role so convincingly that the line between act and truth dissolves over dessert. Elias slips away to photograph deeds in Maren's study. Emotional beat: the fake date turning devastatingly real, and the first crack in Elias's cover.

chapters.title: What the Deeds Say
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias reveals he's an investigator: Aldous Pemberton, the orchard's new owner, is coercing elderly landholders into predatory easements, Maren included. The courts failed a similar case in Maple Hollow years ago. He asks Beatrix to help him gather testimony. Emotional beat: betrayal of the lie giving way to a shared cause — and shared risk.

chapters.title: The Orchard at Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Posing as a couple, they canvass neighbors, and the pretense of intimacy becomes indistinguishable from the real thing — a kiss among the apple trees neither planned. But Pemberton's lawyer spots them asking questions. Emotional beat: falling in love as an act of courage; first external threat.

chapters.title: Maren's Silence
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Maren admits she signed the easement to protect Beatrix from a debt she never knew about, revealing the family's history of quiet sacrifice and the old injustice that broke the town's trust in courts. Beatrix realizes her exile five years ago was partly self-imposed protection from exactly this kind of pain. Emotional beat: inherited wounds surfacing; grandmother and granddaughter reconciling.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Going to Leave
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias's employer — Pemberton's rival developer — wanted dirt, not justice, and orders him to hand over the testimony and go. Elias refuses, burning his professional bridge, but hides it from Beatrix, who discovers a copy of his report addressed to the rival. Emotional beat: the fake relationship's central lie reborn as a real one; trust shattered.

chapters.title: Testimony in the Cider House
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix nearly turns Elias away, but Maren — and the whole town, summoned quietly — gathers in the cider house to hear the truth. The landholders decide to act outside the law that failed them: a public reading of the coerced deeds at the Harvest Festival, with the press invited. Emotional beat: justice as a communal act; Beatrix choosing to trust again.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the festival, the deeds are read aloud before the whole town and a reporter; Pemberton's scheme collapses as witnesses stand one by one. Pemberton confronts Beatrix and Elias privately, threatening to expose their fake relationship — and Beatrix declares it was never fake, in front of everyone. Emotional beat: the climax — public truth, public love, both costing something.

chapters.title: After the Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. With Pemberton gone and the easements voided, Elias prepares to leave on the last train, his work finished. Beatrix, having written the final chapter of her novel the night before, runs to the platform — and finds he never bought a ticket. He asks to stay not as a fake boyfriend but as himself. Emotional beat: belonging chosen freely; the door finally open.
